title: The Secret of My Success
tagline: Mailroom by day. Executive by night.
about: A Kansas farm boy works in the mailroom by day and poses as an executive by night.
cue: Serve the mains when Brantley changes from mailroom clothes to his suit in the lift.
faces: Lean times call for a proper lunch. Charges go to your department. Elevators are not changing rooms.
Mr. Whitfield, new on the executive floor.
Smoked salmon and crème fraîche on warm buckwheat, dill.
Kernels and spring onions in egg batter, fried crisp. Sour cream.
Jumbo shrimp on ice, red sauce.
Iron pan, butter, garlic and thyme.
Buttermilk soaked, fried crisp. Mashed potatoes, gravy.

    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersMail run sandwichHam, cheddar, pickle on white.Comes up on the mail cart at 11.How to make it8 slices of white bread30g butter, softened120g leg ham80g cheddar, sliced50g pickles, thinly slicedButter the bread.Layer the ham, cheddar and pickles across four slices and top with the other slices.Trim off the crusts and cut each sandwich into three fingers.Wrap in baking paper and refrigerate until serving.Kansas corn frittersKernels and spring onions in egg batter, fried crisp. Sour cream.A taste of home, straight off the farm.How to make it2 corn cobs, about 200g of kernels80g plain flour1 tsp baking powder1 egg60ml milk2 spring onions, thinly sliced1/4 tsp salt3 tbsp neutral oil100g sour creamCut the kernels from the cobs.Whisk the flour, baking powder, egg and milk into a thick batter. Stir in the corn, spring onions and salt.Shallow-fry spoonfuls of batter in the neutral oil in batches over medium heat, turning once, until golden and cooked through.Drain and serve with sour cream for dipping.MainsExecutive rib eyeIron pan, butter, garlic and thyme.Charged to your department.How to make it800g rib eye steak, in four pieces1 tsp fine salt1 tbsp neutral oil50g butter4 thyme sprigs3 garlic cloves, lightly crushedPat the steaks dry, salt them evenly and refrigerate uncovered to dry-brine, at least 4 hours.Heat a heavy pan over high heat with the oil.Sear the steaks in batches, turning once.Lower the heat, add the butter, thyme and garlic and baste repeatedly.Rest the steaks, then slice and spoon over the pan butter.SweetsApple pie à la modeCinnamon apples, ice cream.To finish, with coffee by the pot.How to make it400g sweet shortcrust pastry600g Granny Smith apples85g caster sugar1 tsp cinnamon1 egg, beaten200ml vanilla ice creamLine a 20cm pie dish with half the pastry.Peel, core and slice the apples and toss with sugar and cinnamon.Fill the crust, cover with the remaining pastry, crimp, cut steam vents, brush with egg and sprinkle with a little sugar.Bake at 190°C until golden and tender.Rest, then divide into four portions and serve with ice cream.DrinksGin martiniDry vermouth, lemon twist.Bar from 5:30 PM for those working late.How to make it240ml gin40ml dry vermouth400g ice1 lemon, for four thin twistsFreeze four martini glasses.Working in two batches, stir the gin and vermouth with ice.Strain equally into the frozen glasses.Express the lemon twist oils over each drink and garnish.
